rows.l: - Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
- If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
+## How your code is graded (this is the reality you are optimizing for)

+- Your final code is run on the input file you can see, and THEN THE SAME CODE IS AUTOMATICALLY RE-RUN on two more hidden input files for this task. Those files have the same layout but DIFFERENT data — different values, and possibly a different number of data rows — in the same cells and columns. To pass, your one piece of code must produce the correct answer on all three files.

+- Therefore compute every answer FROM THE ACTUAL CELL VALUES your code reads at run time. Never hardcode the output: do not type the answer values in, do not paste the sample result or an example from the instruction, and do not fill a fixed constant (e.g. writing `1` into every row) because it happened to be right for the rows you saw. Read the real data, loop over its real extent (e.g. up to `ws.max_row` or the actual last non-empty row), compute, and write.

+- Only cell VALUES are compared, and only inside answer_position. Cell fill/font colors, number formats, and formula text are NOT graded. So a task that says "highlight" or "format" is still scored on the resulting cell values — put the answer in the values, not only in a color. A live formula counts only by the value it evaluates to (the file is recalculated before grading), so a formula is acceptable only if it will evaluate correctly; when the result is easy to compute in Python, write the literal value instead.
+- The grader compares each cell by its exact value TYPE, so write the correct type:

+  - Dates and times must be written as real Python `datetime`/`date`/`time` objects, NOT as text strings — a date stored as text will never match a real date cell. (The display/number format is irrelevant to grading; the underlying value type is what matters.)
+  - Numeric results must be written as numbers, not as text. Numbers are compared rounded to 2 decimals, and dates are compared to the whole day.
+  - When unsure of the expected type, match the type already used in the sample/answer rows shown or in the adjacent filled cells of the same column.

+- Reference the input file and output_path using the exact path strings you were given (the automatic re-run substitutes the other test files by rewriting those exact names). Do not glob for files or build the path from a hardcoded test-case number.
+## Before you save the final file, verify each item
+1. Every written value is COMPUTED from the input data — nothing is hardcoded from the preview or from an example in the instruction.
+2. Your logic reads the real data extent (not a fixed row count copied from the preview), so it still works when a file has more or fewer rows.
+3. Each written cell has the correct value TYPE (real datetime for dates, number for numeric results, text only for genuine text).
+4. You wrote ONLY inside answer_position; for a Sheet-Level range that is larger than your result, leave the leftover cells blank rather than padding them with guessed values.
+5. You saved to the exact output_path.
